children: Michael Burry (Trades, Portfolio)'s contrarian portfolio took a beating in August as several of his biggest bearish AI bets moved sharply against him, led by
Palantir
, Nvidia
and
Micron Technology

. The famed investor's positioning highlights a growing risk for AI bears: even when valuation concerns look extreme, momentum and earnings growth can keep expensive stocks climbing far longer than skeptics expect.
Seven of the nine stocks Burry was bearish on advanced during August.
Palantir was the biggest problem
, surging more than
even as Burry maintained out-of-the-money put options extending into March 2027 with strike prices in the low-to-mid $100s.
Nvidia added another
during the month. Burry held bearish December 2026 and June 2027 puts while also owning higher-strike December calls, giving him some protection around Nvidia's earnings.
Micron created another headache. Burry had increased his short exposure after arguing that the memory maker's enormous rally reflected speculation more than fundamentals, yet MU shares gained
16.49% in August
Other bearish positions also went the wrong way:
CoreWeave rose 18%, Oracle gained 14.8%, Nebius advanced 8%
, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF added 1.22%.
His long book performed considerably better, although results were mixed.
Veeva Systems
surged
, while
Adobe
climbed 17%. Fannie Mae gained 5.7% and MercadoLibre added 3%.

But PayPal fell 8%, Sprouts Farmers Market lost 6%, and Flutter Entertainment dropped 4%. Burry also remains bullish on Lululemon, which he has described as screaming cheap, and has increased his exposure to JD.com after exiting Alibaba.
Investors Takeaway

August illustrates the difference between identifying valuation risk and successfully timing it. Burry may ultimately be right that parts of the AI trade are overpriced, but Palantir, Nvidia and Micron continue to enjoy powerful earnings and sentiment momentum.
Investors should therefore watch
revenue growth, earnings revisions and valuation multiples

rather than Burry's short positions alone. A meaningful slowdown in AI spending or weaker guidance could rapidly validate his thesis. Until then, his August performance shows why betting against a powerful growth cycle can be painful even when the valuation argument looks compelling.

title: Michael Burry's Biggest AI Bets Take Surprising Turn
